main_body: A central vertical pole (about x=17-22, rows 13-50) with stone stair steps winding around it as wedge-shaped treads, seen largely in side cut
top_band: none on the central pole (only a 1-2px light cap at rows 13-14); the tread wedges are angled slabs, not a clear horizontal top band over a front face
evidence: The main body is the tall central column. A single column through its middle meets a 2px light cap (rows 13-14) and then a shaded vertical shaft down to row 50, which is a rim-only cap with no readable top surface. The steps are shown as a spiral staircase cut from the side, with tilted wedges left and right of the pole. No horizontal surface reads as seen from above, and there is no front edge line, eave shadow or recessed front. It is a side-elevation cut, so it fails the 3/4 contract. The 'structure' kind (gate, pavilion, building) also does not fit well.

style.evidence: The candidate is a grey stone stair with about 4 grey steps. Outlines and the dark gaps between treads are neutral near-black or dark grey with no material tint. The pole and many tread faces are flat fills with no grain, speckle or per-stone shading. Next to the richly textured tile roofs, timber framing and stone walls of the references, it looks much thinner and flatter, and it is not a whole building with roof and walls.
